ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
An electron with mass $m$ and charge magnitude $e$ enters a region of uniform magnetic field above the $x$-axis with velocity $v$ perpendicular to the $x$-axis from a certain point on the $x$-axis. It is known that the magnetic field above the $x$-axis has a magnetic induction strength of $2B$, directed perpendicularly into the plane of the paper, while the magnetic field below the $x$-axis has a magnetic induction strength of $B$, directed perpendicularly out of the plane of the paper. Subsequently, the electron undergoes periodic motion in space.

1. Find the period of the periodic motion of an electron.
2. Find the distance traveled by an electron along the $x$-axis in one period of its motion.

It is known that the magnetic field above the $x$-axis has magnetic induction strength $2B$, directed perpendicularly into the plane of the paper, while the magnetic field below the $x$-axis has magnetic induction strength $B$, directed perpendicularly out of the plane of the paper. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, a horizontal straight line represents the x-axis, and the arrow at the right end is labeled x. An electron starts from a point on the x-axis, and the velocity arrow v is vertically upward, perpendicular to the x-axis. In the region above the x-axis, many crosses are drawn, indicating that the magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface inward, and it is labeled 2B; in the region below the x-axis, many dots are drawn, indicating that the magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface outward, and it is labeled B. Reasoning: The charge of the electron is negative, and the magnitude of the charge is e, so the direction of the Lorentz force is opposite to v×B. When it just enters the upper region, v is upward, B is inward, and v×B is to the left, so the force on the electron is to the right; therefore the upper trajectory bends in the positive x direction. The magnetic induction intensity above is 2B, the radius of circular motion is r_top = mv/(e·2B)=mv/(2eB), and the angular velocity is omega_top = e·2B/m = 2eB/m. After the electron travels a semicircle above, it returns to the x-axis, so the time used is t_top = pi/omega_top = pi m/(2eB), and it advances along the x direction by one diameter 2r_top = mv/(eB). When entering the lower region, the velocity is downward, B is outward, and v×B is to the left, so the force on the electron is still to the right; therefore the lower trajectory also bends in the positive x direction. The magnetic induction intensity below is B, the radius is r_bot = mv/(eB), and the angular velocity is omega_bot = eB/m. After the electron also travels a semicircle below, it returns to the x-axis again, the velocity recovers to upward, and the state of motion is translated relative to the initial state, forming one period. Therefore the time used for the lower semicircle is t_bot = pi/omega_bot = pi m/(eB), and it advances along the x direction by 2r_bot = 2mv/(eB). One period consists of the upper semicircle and the lower semicircle, so T = t_top + t_bot = pi m/(2eB) + pi m/(eB) = 3pi m/(2eB). The distance advanced along the x-axis direction in one period is Delta x = 2r_top + 2r_bot = mv/(eB) + 2mv/(eB) = 3mv/(eB).
